title: `no-check-unified-storage-compatibility` label: when a client/server unified-storage PR can skip the compat check
answers: When can I skip the unified storage compatibility check on a PR?
Do I need to worry about client/server version mismatch for this change?
What does the no-check-unified-storage-compatibility label mean?
body:
Fix pattern/convention: the label is appropriate when a PR touches both apistore/ (client) and resource/ or search/ (server) but each side's change is a local error-handling fix that doesn't move responsibility across the client/server boundary and doesn't touch proto/ or resourcepb/ (the wire contract) — in that case any mix of old/new client and server binaries during a rolling deploy still works.
Constraints: this does not apply if a change alters what resourcepb/proto messages carry, moves a check from server to client (or vice versa), or changes response shape in a way one side relies on the other to interpret — those require the full compatibility check, not the label.

search: The `no-check-unified-storage-compatibility` label is appropriate when a PR spans both pkg/storage/unified/apistore/ (client) and pkg/storage/unified/resource/ or pkg/storage/unified/search/ (server) but each change is a local error-handling fix that does not move responsibility across the client/server boundary and does not touch proto/ or resourcepb/ wire contracts. The constraint is that the label does not apply if the change alters resourcepb/proto messages, moves a check from server to client or vice versa, or changes response shape in a way one side relies on interpreting—those require the full compatibility check. This pattern ensures rolling deploys with mixed old/new binaries remain compatible.
